newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch cooca trade sees no market impact from fire.
newsitem.headline: Dutch cooca trade sees no market impact from fire.

text.p: The loss of 11,000 tonnes of mainly Ivorian cocoa in a warehouse blaze in the Netherlands will have little immediate market impact, Dutch trade sources said on Monday.
"Compared to the amount of cocoa in Amsterdam, it's pretty small. The market is well supplied with material," one said.

The fire at the Unicontrol warehouse in Wormerveer to the north of Amsterdam broke out on Saturday night. A spokesman said the whole warehouse was destroyed and that fire-fighters were still tackling the remnants of the blaze.
He said the owners of the cocoa, mainly destined for the London terminal market, were Phibro, Gerkens and Cacao de Zaan.
It was fully insured, he added.

"There were only a few owners and the main one was Phibro. They were porobably just going to sit on the cocoa for six to nine months anyway. So it won't have any impact," another industry source said.
Cocoa stocks in Amsterdam were estimated by SGS Warehouse Services at the start of this month at around 430,000 tonnes, but some in the trade put the total above 450,000.
Traders said industry buyers for physical cocoa were still thin on the ground and had continued to run down their level of cover from between six and nine months to between three and six.
